name: Effect Datastar TypeScript prototype capability loop

description: Baseline before implementing ts-star prototype; research plan and benchmark script only

asi.hypothesis: Establish a zero-capability baseline and commit the autoresearch harness before adding the first vertical slice.
asi.study_summary: Datastar favors backend-owned state, SSE element/signal patches, fat morphs, sparse signals; strongest borrowed ideas are Stario small SSE helpers, StarHTML typed expression DSL, Hyperlith explicit CQRS/fat morph, Falco typed helpers.

description: First vertical slice attempt failed one HTML expectation around false reactive attr rendering

asi.hypothesis: Add the minimal Datastar SSE, HTML, typed signal/action, Effect signal decoding, and counter handler slice.
asi.error_details: Vitest had 17/18 passing; only html-datastar counter render expected data-attr:disabled=false to be omitted, but renderer correctly treats string attribute value "false" as present because Datastar expressions are strings.
asi.rollback_reason: Failed test run; per autoresearch rules crash logs and reverts the attempted slice.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the slice with the test expectation fixed or remove the dataAttr('disabled', false) from the view. Prefer not emitting the false expression in this fixture because reactive attributes intentionally use string expressions.

description: Implement minimal vertical slice: Datastar SSE encoding, typed signal/action HTML helpers, Effect Schema signal decoding, and counter handler

asi.hypothesis: A small pure core plus Effect Schema request decoding can prove the framework shape without committing to JSX, routers, or CQRS machinery.
asi.learned: The minimal slice is coherent: golden-like SSE strings, typed signal refs, HTML rendering, Web Request signal parsing, and Effect handlers all compose in tests. Reactive data-* expression values are strings even when the expression is false; omit attrs only for HTML boolean false, not Datastar expression strings.
architecture_validated: pure sse.ts wire encoder is easy to golden-test
datastar.ts expression/attribute helpers provide type safety without much ceremony
request.ts can decode GET query and POST body signals with Effect Schema
vertical counter handler can stay a plain Effect returning a Web Response
asi.next_action_hint: Add a stronger compile-time type-safety test for signal value operations, plus exact comparisons against more included SDK fixtures such as namespace/multiline signal and remove signal cases.

description: Expand Datastar protocol coverage with more SDK fixtures and compile-time signal safety checks

asi.hypothesis: The direct SSE encoder should match additional official SDK fixtures, and the typed Signal API should reject common misuse at TypeScript compile time.
asi.learned: executeScript is a datastar-patch-elements event with mode append before selector body, unlike general patchElements option ordering. removeSignals is just patchSignals with null leaves, including nested dot paths. @ts-expect-error tests confirm number/boolean signal operation constraints and declared signal-record keys.
asi.next_action_hint: Prototype a small Effect-aware route abstraction or CQRS live stream helper next, but keep it thin and explicit. Consider adding exact server example using Node's Web Request/Response before any router abstraction.

description: Thin Effect handler/router attempt failed typecheck due Headers.entries lib typing and duplicate HttpMethod export

asi.hypothesis: Add a minimal exact router and withSignals helper without introducing full framework routing abstractions.
asi.error_details: tsc failed before tests: Headers.entries is missing from current lib typing in this configuration, and index.ts wildcard exports caused duplicate HttpMethod from datastar.ts and handler.ts.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with Array.from(new Headers(...)) or forEach instead of entries, and rename handler HttpMethod to RouteMethod or avoid wildcard conflict.

description: Add thin Effect handler utilities with typed signal decoding and exact-route dispatch

asi.hypothesis: A tiny Handler type, withSignals helper, and exact router can improve DX while keeping routing explicit and reversible.
asi.learned: The handler layer can stay very small: Web Request to Effect<Response>, exact route matching, built-in 404/405, and withSignals composition. Avoided middleware/params. Type issue fixed by renaming handler method type to RouteMethod and using Headers directly instead of entries.
asi.next_action_hint: Next useful slice is Node runtime adapter or realtime/CQRS helper. Prefer Node adapter first so the vertical slice can run under node:http with Web Request/Response semantics.

description: Node adapter attempt failed typecheck on Buffer BodyInit and overly strict createNodeListener requirements

asi.hypothesis: Add a Node http adapter around the Web Request/Response handler model.
asi.error_details: tsc failed: Buffer<ArrayBufferLike> not assignable to DOM BodyInit, and createNodeListener accepted Handler<unknown, never> so tests with Handler<any, any> were rejected.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply using body.buffer.slice(...) or Uint8Array ArrayBuffer-safe conversion, and make createNodeListener accept Handler<unknown, any> or Handler<unknown, never> with a less restrictive R type.

description: Add Node http adapter for Web Request/Response Effect handlers

asi.hypothesis: A Node runtime adapter can keep the framework API on Web Request/Response while still targeting node:http.
asi.learned: The adapter works with real node:http + fetch tests: exact route serving, POST body signal decoding, router 404s, default 500s, and custom error responses. TypeScript DOM BodyInit does not accept Buffer directly, so body conversion uses an ArrayBuffer slice. createNodeListener currently casts Handler requirements to never, so handlers needing services should be provided before adaptation.
asi.tradeoff: This is intentionally a boundary adapter, not a server abstraction. It avoids taking over listen/lifecycle concerns for now.
asi.next_action_hint: Next explore realtime/CQRS helper as an optional pattern: a small in-process broadcaster or stream response that sends fat morph patches from Effect Streams.

description: Add optional realtime helpers for broadcaster-backed Datastar SSE streams

asi.hypothesis: Realtime can be modeled as a tiny optional primitive: publish values, map them to fat-morph element patches, and stream them as text/event-stream responses.
asi.learned: A minimal Broadcaster + AsyncIterable bridge is enough to prove the CQRS/live-update shape without introducing a complex sync engine. The API remains explicit: app code decides what values to publish and how to render them to Datastar patches.
asi.tradeoff: This broadcaster is in-process and not production durable; it is a prototype pattern. For real deployment, the same AsyncIterable shape could wrap NATS/Redis/Postgres notifications.
asi.next_action_hint: Add a README/example that explains the current architecture and demonstrates the counter plus live stream. Documentation is now valuable because the prototype has several coherent primitives.

description: Document architecture and add tested counter example

asi.hypothesis: Now that core primitives are coherent, a README and executable counter example will improve DX clarity and serve as a regression fixture.
asi.learned: The architecture can be explained compactly as pure SSE, typed Datastar helpers, tiny HTML rendering, Effect Schema request decoding, plain Effect handlers, Node adapter, and optional realtime helpers. The counter example exercises these without adding framework-level generalization.
asi.next_action_hint: Improve templating ergonomics next. Either add a safer attr-fragment API for common Datastar patterns or test a small JSX factory experiment; keep it reversible.

description: JSX templating experiment failed typecheck on children typing and fragment factory shape

asi.hypothesis: A classic JSX factory can be a reversible templating alternative over the existing HTML node model.
asi.error_details: TSX failed: IntrinsicElements index signature did not allow JSX children arrays, and Fragment as a Symbol was not accepted as a JSX element type for <> fragments.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with a callable/string Fragment marker and broader JSX children typing, e.g. allow children?: any and AttributeValue | Child in JSX attributes, or skip <> fragment support initially.

description: Fixed JSX fragment typing attempt still failed narrowing callable Fragment vs string tag

asi.hypothesis: A callable Fragment and broader JSX attr typing should make classic JSX work over the HTML model.
asi.error_details: tsc still failed: after checking tag === Fragment, TypeScript did not narrow JsxTag to string for h(tag,...).
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with an explicit typeof tag === 'string' branch (or cast tag as string after the Fragment branch).

description: JSX factory typechecked but tests failed because transform injected __self and __source attrs

asi.hypothesis: A classic JSX factory with callable Fragment can render through existing HTML nodes.
asi.error_details: Vitest/TSX transform passed __self and __source props into the factory, and renderer emitted them as HTML attributes in all JSX tests.
asi.rollback_reason: Test failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Filter dev-only JSX props (__self, __source) in the jsx factory before passing attrs to h().

description: JSX factory experiment passed but primary metric did not improve because benchmark ignored .tsx tests

asi.hypothesis: A classic JSX factory can be a reversible templating alternative over the existing HTML node model.
asi.learned: The JSX factory now works after filtering dev-only __self/__source props and using a callable Fragment. However the autoresearch primary metric script only counts .test.ts/.spec.ts files, so the new passing .tsx tests were invisible to prototype_score even though vitest reported 45 passing tests.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric was unchanged at 42; per autoresearch rules equal primary metrics are discarded. The benchmark definition needs to be fixed to count .tsx tests before reattempting JSX.
asi.next_action_hint: First update autoresearch.sh to count .test.tsx/.spec.tsx in prototype_score, then reapply the JSX factory and tests so the metric reflects the intended capability count without overfitting.

description: Add reversible JSX templating experiment and count TSX tests in prototype score

asi.hypothesis: JSX can be offered as a thin optional templating layer over the existing HTML node model without changing the core architecture.
asi.learned: Classic JSX works after using a callable Fragment, broad JSX attr typing, explicit string tag cast, and filtering dev-only __self/__source props. The benchmark now correctly counts .test.tsx/.spec.tsx tests, aligning prototype_score with the stated metric of passing prototype test cases rather than only .ts tests.
asi.tradeoff: JSX is currently just a reversible factory over h()/render(); Datastar attr fragments still come from helper spreads, so this does not commit to a React-like component model or client framework.
asi.next_action_hint: Next most promising improvement is better Datastar DX around typed attributes/options: add helper builders for event modifiers (debounce, delay, once) and action options, or add safer signal name validation.

description: Add typed Datastar event modifier helpers for common timing and listener suffixes

asi.hypothesis: Typed modifier builders will improve Datastar DX without adding magic, by making documented suffix syntax easier and less error-prone.
asi.learned: The helper API can cover data-on, data-on-intersect, data-on-interval, and data-on-signal-patch with simple object options. Tags must be grouped on one modifier suffix (for example __debounce.500ms.leading, not repeated __debounce segments). For data-on, target/control modifiers before timing produces documented examples like __window__debounce.500ms.leading.
asi.next_action_hint: Add safer signal-name/path validation next. Current signal(name) accepts arbitrary strings at runtime; a small runtime validator plus typed constructor can catch invalid Datastar signal names early without changing app architecture.

description: Signal name validation attempt failed typecheck because Error has name property

asi.hypothesis: Add runtime validation for signal names/paths and dataSignals keys to catch malformed Datastar interactions early.
asi.error_details: tsc failed: SignalNameError constructor used a parameter property named `name`, which overrides Error.name under noImplicitOverride and requires an override modifier.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with the field renamed to signalName (or explicit override if desired).

description: Validate Datastar signal names and dataSignals keys at runtime

asi.hypothesis: Early runtime validation of signal names will prevent confusing Datastar case conversion/addressing bugs without adding architectural complexity.
asi.learned: Signal constructor and path() can validate dot-separated JS-identifier-like paths, including local underscore-prefixed signals. dataSignals can recursively validate object keys while leaving Expr values alone. Renaming SignalNameError.name to signalName avoids conflict with Error.name under noImplicitOverride.
asi.tradeoff: The validator intentionally rejects hyphenated signal names even though Datastar can case-convert some attributes, because typed server helpers should prefer explicit stable signal paths.
asi.next_action_hint: Add typed response helpers for HTML response header variants and Datastar text/html/json direct response modes, or add a static Datastar client asset helper for serving datastar.js in the Node adapter.

description: Datastar client asset helper attempt failed typecheck because Uint8Array is not DOM BodyInit

asi.hypothesis: Add explicit helpers for rendering and serving the self-hosted Datastar client script.
asi.error_details: tsc failed: Response constructor BodyInit typing in this config does not accept Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> directly.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply converting Uint8Array to an ArrayBuffer slice (same lesson as Node adapter Buffer body conversion) or restrict datastarClientResponse to string.

description: Add Datastar client script and asset-serving helpers

asi.hypothesis: Since Datastar's browser script is a core runtime asset, ts-star should make self-hosting it explicit and easy to test.
asi.learned: A small client.ts can cover script tag rendering, CDN fallback, static script responses, in-memory routes, and file-backed routes for the included minified datastar.js. Uint8Array response bodies need ArrayBuffer slice conversion under the current DOM typings.
asi.tradeoff: The helper does not bundle/copy datastar.js or assume a deployment layout; apps still decide whether to use CDN, in-memory content, or a file route.
asi.next_action_hint: Improve response ergonomics next: Datastar can also consume direct text/html and application/json responses with Datastar headers. Add helpers for html patch headers and json signal patch headers, not just SSE.

description: Add direct Datastar action response helpers for HTML, JSON signals, and scripts

asi.hypothesis: Datastar apps should not be forced into SSE for single-shot actions; helpers for documented direct response content types improve framework completeness and DX.
asi.learned: Direct response helpers are straightforward: text/html uses datastar-selector/mode/use-view-transition headers, application/json uses datastar-only-if-missing, and text/javascript uses datastar-script-attributes. This complements SSE helpers without changing handler architecture.
asi.next_action_hint: Next useful slice: improve request decoding for form mode or query/body edge cases, e.g. DELETE uses query signals like GET, empty POST body defaults to {}, malformed JSON reports SignalJsonError.

description: Request edge-case tests failed because Effect.runPromise wraps failures in FiberFailure

asi.hypothesis: Harden request decoding around Datastar request headers, DELETE query signals, empty bodies, raw payloads, and malformed JSON errors.
asi.error_details: Only failing test expected runPromise rejection to be instanceof SignalJsonError, but Effect.runPromise rejects with a FiberFailure wrapper around the typed error.
asi.rollback_reason: Test failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply using Effect.either(readSignals(...)) in the malformed JSON test to inspect the typed error channel directly.

description: Harden Datastar request helpers for headers and signal payload edge cases

asi.hypothesis: Request decoding should cover documented Datastar request mechanics and expose small utilities for framework/app code.
asi.learned: GET and DELETE use query signals, empty non-GET bodies should decode as {}, rawSignalsFromRequest remains useful for custom decoders, and typed Effect failures should be tested via Effect.either instead of expecting runPromise to reject with the raw error. isDatastarRequest is a simple header check for Datastar-Request: true.
asi.next_action_hint: Next promising slice: add route params or query decoding? Be careful: route params add router complexity. Prefer query decoding with Effect Schema, since Datastar examples often use query resources and it stays small.

description: Query decoding attempt failed typecheck due readonly-array narrowing

asi.hypothesis: Add small query parameter decoding with Effect Schema while deferring route params.
asi.error_details: tsc failed in queryFromRequest: TypeScript did not narrow QueryValue to string in the non-array branch because QueryValue includes ReadonlyArray<string>.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply using `const existingValues = typeof existing === 'string' ? [existing] : existing` or an explicit cast in the else branch.

description: Add Effect Schema query parameter decoding helpers

asi.hypothesis: Typed query decoding is useful for Datastar resource endpoints and keeps routing explicit without introducing path params yet.
asi.learned: queryFromRequest can preserve normal params as strings and repeated params as arrays; readQuery composes that with Effect Schema, including NumberFromString parsing and typed schema failures. Avoid route params for now to keep router simple.
asi.next_action_hint: Next: add small route composition ergonomics (prefix or concat) rather than params. Prefixing supports grouping /api or /examples while staying exact-route and simple.

description: Route composition helper attempt failed typecheck because concatRoutes widened route requirements to any

asi.hypothesis: Add prefix/concat route composition helpers while preserving exact-route semantics and avoiding path params.
asi.error_details: Tests failed typecheck: concatRoutes returned routes widened to Route<any, any>, making router return an Effect with any requirements that Effect.runPromise rejected under exactOptionalPropertyTypes.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply prefixRoutes only first, or type concatRoutes with a simpler generic that preserves each group element union without widening to any; alternatively use router(...health, ...api) and skip concatRoutes.

description: Add exact-route prefixing helper for route group assembly

asi.hypothesis: Route prefixing is a small ergonomic win for grouping Datastar endpoints while preserving the explicit exact-route model.
asi.learned: prefixRoutes works without introducing path params, nested routers, or middleware. A broader concatRoutes helper widened route types to any and was discarded; route groups can be spread directly for now.
asi.tradeoff: This intentionally avoids dynamic params. Query decoding plus exact paths remains simpler and aligned with the exploratory scope.
asi.next_action_hint: Next potential DX improvement: typed HTML attribute merging could catch collisions or support conditional attrs, but be cautious not to over-abstract.

description: Strict attribute merge tests failed because dataAttr string values are JSON string literals

asi.hypothesis: Offer strict attribute merging to catch accidental collisions while keeping permissive mergeAttrs for overrides.
asi.error_details: Only failing test expected dataAttr('disabled', '$saving') to emit $saving, but string inputs are intentionally JSON-quoted expressions. Need raw('$saving') or a Signal for Datastar expression values.
asi.rollback_reason: Test failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with raw('$saving') in the test for expression-valued dataAttr.

description: Add strict attribute merging for collision-sensitive Datastar fragments

asi.hypothesis: Attribute collision detection is useful when composing many Datastar attr fragments; a strict merge helper can catch mistakes without removing the permissive override merge.
asi.learned: mergeAttrs remains override-friendly, while mergeAttrsStrict throws AttributeConflictError on duplicate keys and works for independent Datastar fragments. Tests should use raw('$saving') or Signal values for Datastar expressions; plain strings are intentionally JSON string literals.
asi.next_action_hint: Next useful iteration: add docs/examples for choosing builder vs JSX and strict vs permissive attrs, or add more expression DSL helpers such as conditional/and/or to reduce raw JavaScript strings.

description: Add minimal Datastar expression combinators

asi.hypothesis: Small expression combinators can improve type-safe Datastar DX without turning the prototype into a full expression language.
asi.learned: not/and/or/ternary cover common conditional attribute/text use cases and compose cleanly with Signal, raw, dataClass, dataAttr, and text. Empty and/or use logical identities to keep generated expressions predictable.
asi.tradeoff: This stays intentionally tiny; no method-chain string/array DSL yet. Further expression work should be motivated by examples, not completeness.
asi.next_action_hint: Add a fuller example using query decoding + direct responses or realtime helper, to validate primitives compose beyond the counter.

description: Add search example with dynamic Datastar URL, query decoding, and direct HTML patches

asi.hypothesis: A second vertical example will validate that the primitives compose beyond a counter and reveal whether direct HTML patch responses feel coherent.
asi.learned: Dynamic URL expressions fit naturally by allowing get/post/etc. to accept Expr<string>. The search example composes dataSignals, bind, debounced data-on, readQuery, htmlPatchResponse, and exact routes without adding new framework abstractions. This demonstrates a non-SSE single-shot Datastar action path.
asi.tradeoff: The dynamic URL still uses raw template literal JavaScript; a safer URL builder may be worth exploring later if examples repeat this pattern.
asi.next_action_hint: Potential next step: a typed URL/query expression helper for dynamic action URLs, or a live example using Broadcaster to prove realtime composition in an example file.

description: Add encoded queryUrl helper for dynamic Datastar action URLs

asi.hypothesis: A small URL expression helper can remove raw JavaScript template literals from common dynamic @get URLs while preserving explicit Datastar expressions.
asi.learned: queryUrl composes with signal refs and static values to produce encoded template-literal URLs, and get/post/etc. can accept Expr<string> URLs. The search example now uses queryUrl instead of raw URL JavaScript.
asi.tradeoff: queryUrl does not handle optional/removable params yet; it intentionally covers the common stable-query case only.
asi.next_action_hint: A live realtime example using Broadcaster would validate the remaining realtime primitives in examples, but avoid expanding into a sync engine.

description: Live counter example failed typecheck due Handler namespace/type export collision

asi.hypothesis: A live counter example can validate Broadcaster + liveElementsResponse realtime composition without introducing a sync engine.
asi.error_details: examples/live-counter.ts imported `type Handler` from index, but index also exports `Handler` namespace, causing TS2709 Cannot use namespace 'Handler' as a type. Downstream test values became unknown.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply importing `type Handler` directly from `../src/handler.js`, not from index.

description: Add live counter example backed by Broadcaster SSE patches

asi.hypothesis: A live example should prove the realtime primitives compose into a Datastar CQRS-style flow without adding a sync engine.
asi.learned: createLiveCounter demonstrates page init opening /live, POST /increment mutating server state and publishing, and liveElementsResponse streaming fat-morph output patches. Broadcaster.closeAll is useful for stream lifecycle/tests. Importing type Handler from index collides with the Handler namespace export; example imports it from handler.ts directly.
asi.tradeoff: State is in-process and intentionally toy-level. The example validates architecture, not production persistence or distributed fanout.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider cleaning the public index export to avoid Handler namespace/type collision, e.g. rename namespace export to HandlerModule or remove namespace exports if wildcard exports are enough.

description: Fix public index Handler type collision by renaming namespace export

asi.hypothesis: The public package root should allow importing the Handler type directly without colliding with a namespace export.
asi.learned: Renaming the namespace export from Handler to Handlers preserves grouped helper access while allowing `import type { Handler } from '../src/index.js'`. This avoids the type issue hit in the live-counter example.
asi.tradeoff: Plural namespace is slightly less symmetrical with other namespace exports, but it is clearer and avoids type/value namespace ambiguity.
asi.next_action_hint: Update README public API notes or add package-root usage examples to reinforce the intended imports.

description: Add handler error mapping for explicit HTTP responses

asi.hypothesis: Effect handlers should keep typed failures in the error channel but need an ergonomic boundary helper for mapping those failures to HTTP responses.
asi.learned: mapErrorResponse composes with plain handlers, withSignals decode failures, and exact routes. This lets apps turn schema/request errors into 400s without moving error handling into the Node adapter or router.
asi.tradeoff: The mapper returns a synchronous Response only; effectful error recovery can be added later if a concrete need appears.
asi.next_action_hint: Potential next slice: add a small NotFound/BadRequest error response helper set or leave app-specific. More valuable may be documenting the current prototype architecture thoroughly.

description: Add explicit empty response helper for command endpoints

asi.hypothesis: Command endpoints commonly return 204/202; an explicit helper improves readability without adding framework policy.
asi.learned: emptyResponse covers 204 defaults and alternate empty statuses/headers, and makes the live counter increment handler clearer than ad-hoc Response construction.
asi.tradeoff: Kept this minimal; no broad response factory hierarchy.
asi.next_action_hint: At this point core prototype is broad. Consider adding architecture notes/tradeoffs to README or autoresearch ideas rather than continuing to add tiny helpers.

description: Add object-form Datastar data-attr and data-class helpers

asi.hypothesis: Object-form binding helpers improve DX for multiple attributes/classes and special CSS class names without expanding the expression DSL.
asi.learned: dataAttrs and dataClasses serialize expression mappings into Datastar-compatible object expressions with quoted keys. This covers multi-attribute bindings and Tailwind-style class names containing ':' or '/' that are awkward as keyed attributes.
asi.tradeoff: Single-key dataAttr/dataClass remain for clarity. Object-form helper does not try to preserve base classes automatically; examples should decide class composition explicitly.
asi.next_action_hint: Possible next slice: add dataStyle/dataStyles helpers or stop and document. data-style is in Datastar docs and complements attrs/classes.

description: Add Datastar data-style helper family

asi.hypothesis: Style bindings are part of Datastar's core attribute set and should mirror the single-key/object-form helper pattern used for attrs and classes.
asi.learned: dataStyle/dataStyles compose with signals and ternary expressions, completing a small consistent helper family: dataAttr(s), dataClass(es), dataStyle(s).
asi.tradeoff: No CSS object normalization or camel/kebab conversion yet; helper stays explicit and close to Datastar syntax.
asi.next_action_hint: Now the attr helper surface is broader. Consider writing a compact reference table in README, but a pure docs commit won't improve primary metric unless paired with examples/tests.

description: Signal patch filter helper tests failed due incorrect expected regex literal

asi.hypothesis: Fill the helper gap around data-on-signal-patch-filter and compose it with signal patch listeners.
asi.error_details: Only failing test expected regex('^draft') to render /^draft without trailing slash; actual helper correctly renders /^draft/.
asi.rollback_reason: Test expectation failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with expected '{"include": /^draft/}'.

description: Add Datastar signal patch filter helper

asi.hypothesis: Signal patch filters are part of Datastar's reactive attribute surface and should compose with onSignalPatch helpers.
asi.learned: onSignalPatchFilter serializes include/exclude regex expressions into data-on-signal-patch-filter. It composes cleanly with onSignalPatch and strict attr merging. Regex helper always emits full /pattern/ literal syntax.
asi.next_action_hint: Potential next slice: add ref/jsonSignals/preserveAttr helpers to cover more documented Datastar attributes, but weigh against scope creep.

description: Add helpers for data-ref, data-json-signals, and data-preserve-attr

asi.hypothesis: A few remaining simple Datastar attributes can be covered with thin helpers, improving self-documenting DX without new abstractions.
asi.learned: ref validates signal names and supports Signal inputs, jsonSignals handles inspector filters and terse mode, and preserveAttr is just a space-joined attr list. These stay close to Datastar syntax.
asi.tradeoff: Still not aiming for exhaustive Datastar attribute coverage; only adding low-cost primitives already used in docs/examples.
asi.next_action_hint: Could add data-ignore/data-ignore-morph helpers next, but consider whether the attr surface is becoming broad enough for this prototype.

description: Add Datastar ignore and ignore-morph helpers

asi.hypothesis: data-ignore and data-ignore-morph are low-cost helpers for explicit Datastar boundaries, useful when integrating third-party DOM or preserving morph-sensitive islands.
asi.learned: ignore(), ignore({self:true}), and ignoreMorph() cover the documented attributes with no extra abstraction. The attribute helper surface is now broad enough for the prototype; further expansion risks chasing completeness.
asi.next_action_hint: Shift from adding helpers to writing concise architecture notes or refactoring docs. If metrics require code/tests, consider tests around examples staying importable from package root rather than new API surface.

description: Allow HTML response helpers to render HTML nodes directly

asi.hypothesis: Response helpers should accept the framework's HTML nodes directly so app handlers don't need manual render(...) calls everywhere.
asi.learned: htmlResponse and htmlPatchResponse can take either raw HTML strings or HtmlNode/Child values. Strings remain raw for existing code, while nodes are rendered and escaped through the HTML renderer. Direct Datastar HTML patches now compose more ergonomically with h()/JSX output.
asi.tradeoff: String input remains raw HTML, so callers must still avoid passing untrusted strings as HTML. Node input is the safer path for generated content.
asi.next_action_hint: Update examples to use node-accepting htmlResponse/htmlPatchResponse directly, or leave as is to avoid churn. Another useful slice: expose a `renderPage`/doctype helper if examples keep hand-building full documents.

description: Add minimal HTML document helper

asi.hypothesis: Examples need full HTML pages often enough that a tiny doctype/document helper is clearer than hand-written strings.
asi.learned: htmlDocument composes the existing h()/render pipeline with doctype, lang, head, and body children, including datastarScript in head. It remains templating-agnostic and does not introduce a component system.
asi.tradeoff: Very small helper; no meta defaults, asset management, or layout abstraction. Good for examples but not a full page framework.
asi.next_action_hint: Update examples to use htmlDocument only if paired with tests or further example cleanup; otherwise consider adding README architecture summary outside metric loop.

description: Add Node serve and close helpers for Effect handlers

asi.hypothesis: A minimal serve helper improves prototype runability while preserving the Web Request/Response handler model and avoiding a larger server framework.
asi.learned: serve(app) wraps createNodeListener with node:http listen defaults (127.0.0.1, ephemeral port), closeServer gives tests/apps an Effectful shutdown, and serverOrigin makes fetch-based tests straightforward.
asi.tradeoff: No scoped resource layer or CLI yet; this is a minimal start/close helper. Effect.scoped could be explored later if lifecycle needs grow.
asi.next_action_hint: Update examples to export runnable main or add package scripts only if needed. Otherwise focus on architecture docs and reviewing accumulated API for overreach.

description: Scoped server helper failed typecheck because acquireRelease release action could fail

asi.hypothesis: Add an Effect.scoped server helper using acquireRelease for idiomatic lifecycle management.
asi.error_details: Effect.acquireRelease requires the release action to be infallible, but closeServer returns Effect<void, Error>.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with release `(server) => Effect.orDie(closeServer(server))` or catch all close errors in the finalizer.

description: Add scoped Node server helper for Effect lifecycles

asi.hypothesis: A scoped server helper fits Effect-style resource management better than only returning a manually closed Server.
asi.learned: serveScoped uses Effect.acquireRelease around serve/closeServer and must make the finalizer infallible, so close errors are orDie'd. Tests can fetch within Effect.scoped and rely on automatic cleanup.
asi.tradeoff: Close failures become defects in scoped finalization. This is acceptable for a prototype; richer lifecycle error handling can wait for concrete needs.
asi.next_action_hint: Now that server lifecycle exists, examples could expose small runnable entrypoints, but adding CLI/package scripts may be premature.

description: Make examples return full Datastar documents

asi.hypothesis: Now that Node serve/scoped lifecycle helpers exist, examples should return full Datastar HTML documents with the client script rather than only fragments, so they are closer to runnable prototypes.
asi.learned: counter/search/live examples can share htmlDocument + datastarScript while preserving existing fragment helpers for tests and patches. Search and live root pages now include the Datastar client script instead of only returning a main fragment.
asi.tradeoff: Kept examples on the default local /datastar.js script path and did not add package scripts or CLI entrypoints yet; serving the client asset remains explicit for apps to wire as needed.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider adding a tiny appRoutes/pageRoutes composition helper for pairing root pages with datastarClientRoute, or improve SSE patch responses to accept HTML nodes like direct HTML responses.

description: Allow SSE patch element responses to render HTML nodes

asi.hypothesis: SSE patch element responses should accept the same rendered HTML node inputs as direct HTML responses, reducing manual render(...) calls for streamed Datastar patches.
asi.learned: patchElementsResponse can reuse the response layer's HtmlContent rendering while keeping the lower-level sse.patchElements encoder pure string-based. Node inputs are escaped through the HTML renderer before becoming SSE data lines.
asi.tradeoff: The low-level SSE encoder still accepts strings only, preserving wire-focused purity and avoiding a dependency from sse.ts to the templating layer.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider updating examples/live-counter countFragment to return an HTML node directly, or add a small helper to pair a full page route with a Datastar client asset route.

description: Add Datastar document and page response helpers

asi.hypothesis: Factoring the repeated htmlResponse(htmlDocument({ head: datastarScript(), body })) pattern into Datastar document/page helpers will keep runnable pages explicit while reducing ceremony in examples.
asi.learned: datastarDocument and datastarPageResponse compose existing htmlDocument, datastarScript, and htmlResponse helpers without adding routing policy. Counter/search/live examples can now return full Datastar pages through a single helper while retaining fragment/node functions for patches and tests.
asi.tradeoff: The helper only injects the script tag and document shell; it does not automatically serve /datastar.js or introduce an app/router wrapper. Asset routing remains explicit via datastarClientRoute/datastarClientFileRoute.
asi.next_action_hint: Next consider adding a tiny route helper that pairs app routes with a Datastar client asset route, or update live-counter countFragment to return an HTML node directly now that patch streaming accepts nodes end-to-end.

description: Make live counter patches node-based end-to-end

asi.hypothesis: Now that realtime and SSE patch response helpers render HTML nodes, the live counter example should return a node fragment directly instead of pre-rendering to a string.
asi.learned: liveElementsResponse already accepts Child values, so countFragment can stay as an HtmlNode and the broadcaster stream still emits the same Datastar patch-elements SSE. This keeps fragments composable for reuse in pages, patches, and tests.
asi.tradeoff: The example still renders pageView to a string for simple fixture assertions; deeper component/page factoring is deferred.
asi.next_action_hint: Next consider explicit Datastar client asset route composition for examples so the full pages that load /datastar.js also serve that route when run under node.

description: Add helper for pairing app routes with Datastar client asset route

asi.hypothesis: Full Datastar pages load /datastar.js, so prototypes need a small explicit way to pair exact app routes with the client asset route without hiding asset serving or adding a framework wrapper.
asi.learned: datastarClientRoutes(script, ...routes) prepends the default /datastar.js route and composes directly with the existing exact-route router. This keeps asset serving explicit and verifies a page route plus client route can be dispatched together.
asi.tradeoff: The helper intentionally only handles in-memory script content and the default path; file-backed assets remain explicit through datastarClientFileRoute to avoid overloading the route composition API too early.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider a file-backed companion helper only if examples start wiring the real ../datastar.js asset repeatedly; otherwise improve diagnostics around missing client asset or route/method errors.

description: Stream Web Response bodies through the Node adapter

asi.hypothesis: The Node adapter must stream Web Response bodies chunk-by-chunk because buffering response.arrayBuffer() prevents long-lived Datastar SSE/live responses from delivering events under node:http.
asi.learned: writeWebResponse can use Response.body.getReader() and write each Uint8Array to ServerResponse as it arrives, preserving headers and backpressure via drain. A node:http fetch test now observes the first SSE chunk before the response body closes.
asi.tradeoff: The adapter remains intentionally small: no advanced abort propagation or custom high-watermark handling yet. Stream errors still surface through the existing listener error path.
asi.next_action_hint: Next consider abort propagation from closed Node clients to Web stream readers/subscriptions, or add a runnable live-counter Node test that proves Broadcaster SSE works through serve().

description: Flush Node streaming headers before first body chunk

asi.hypothesis: Datastar SSE clients should receive response headers and establish the stream even when the first event is delayed, so the Node adapter should flush headers before reading streaming body chunks.
asi.learned: Calling ServerResponse.flushHeaders() after setting response headers and before reading the Web Response body lets fetch resolve on headers before the first async event is produced. This avoids deadlocks for live streams that wait for later publishes.
asi.tradeoff: Headers are committed before the stream body completes, so later stream failures cannot change the HTTP status. That is normal for long-lived SSE responses and matches the explicit streaming boundary.
asi.next_action_hint: Add an integration test for the live-counter example through serve() to verify a broadcaster-backed Datastar stream works over real node:http with header flushing and chunk streaming.

description: Verify live counter SSE through node:http serve helper

asi.hypothesis: After adding chunk streaming and header flushing to the Node adapter, a real broadcaster-backed live counter should stream Datastar SSE updates through serve() over node:http.
asi.learned: The live counter example can be served with serve(liveCounter.app), fetch /live to establish an SSE stream, POST /increment over the same Node app, and receive a patch-elements event over the network before closing the broadcaster subscription.
asi.tradeoff: This is an integration test rather than new API surface. It validates the runtime boundary without adding a broader server framework or CLI entrypoint.
asi.next_action_hint: Next consider propagating client disconnects/abort signals to subscriptions so long-lived Broadcaster streams are cleaned up when a browser closes the SSE connection.

description: SSE disconnect cleanup attempt failed because node:http client cancel did not close subscription

asi.hypothesis: Propagate SSE response cancellation to async iterators/subscriptions so long-lived broadcaster streams are cleaned up when clients disconnect.
asi.error_details: Unit-level response-body cancellation likely worked, but the node:http integration test still observed broadcaster.size() === 1 after fetch body reader.cancel(). The server-side close signal was not sufficient or not observed by the adapter within the polling window.
asi.rollback_reason: Test failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply a smaller slice first: keep eventStreamResponse cancel/Subscription.return with a unit test, and defer node/http disconnect propagation until a reliable abort signal strategy is designed.

description: Cancel SSE async iterators when response bodies are canceled

asi.hypothesis: A smaller reliable cancellation primitive should close async iterators/subscriptions when an SSE Response body itself is canceled, even if full node/http disconnect propagation needs more design.
asi.learned: eventStreamResponse can be implemented with a pull/cancel ReadableStream and an explicit async iterator. BroadcastSubscription now implements return() by closing itself, so canceling the Response body releases the broadcaster subscription at the pure Web Response boundary.
asi.tradeoff: This does not yet prove that every Node client disconnect reaches the Web Response cancel path; the prior node/http integration attempt was flaky/ineffective. The reliable primitive is still useful for controlled cancellation and future adapter work.
asi.next_action_hint: Revisit Node disconnect propagation by passing an AbortSignal from IncomingMessage/ServerResponse into writeWebResponse or by testing with a lower-level HTTP client instead of fetch reader.cancel().

description: Cancel Node streaming response readers on client socket close

asi.hypothesis: Node disconnect cleanup can be made reliable by listening to ServerResponse.close and canceling the Web Response reader, while testing with a lower-level node:http client that actually destroys the socket instead of fetch reader.cancel().
asi.learned: writeWebResponse now cancels the Web response reader when ServerResponse emits close, which lets eventStreamResponse invoke iterator.return() and release subscriptions. A node:http client destroying the response verifies the server observes the disconnect and cancels the never-ending SSE iterator.
asi.tradeoff: This handles the Node adapter boundary but still does not expose a request AbortSignal to app handlers. Chunk writes now also reject if the response closes before drain, keeping the streaming loop from hanging.
asi.next_action_hint: Next consider exposing request abort/cancellation to handlers if app effects need cleanup beyond response-body streams; otherwise improve route diagnostics or typed response error helpers.

description: Abort Web Request signals on Node client disconnect

asi.hypothesis: Once ServerResponse.close is observed in the Node adapter, the same disconnect should also abort the Web Request.signal so handlers can clean up app-level effects beyond response stream iterator cancellation.
asi.learned: createNodeListener now creates an AbortController per request, passes its signal into nodeRequestToWeb, and aborts it on ServerResponse.close. A low-level node:http client destroying an SSE response verifies handlers can observe request.signal abort.
asi.tradeoff: The signal aborts on response close, including normal completion after the handler boundary. This is acceptable for Web Request semantics at the adapter edge; long-running handlers can use it for disconnect cleanup, while completed handlers ignore it.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider adding a tiny helper to turn Request.signal into an Effect interruption/abort primitive, or shift to docs explaining streaming/disconnect lifecycle now that runtime behavior is covered.

description: Add Effect helpers for awaiting request abort signals

asi.hypothesis: Handlers should be able to compose client-disconnect cleanup in Effect without writing raw AbortSignal event-listener boilerplate.
asi.learned: waitForAbortSignal and waitForRequestAbort expose AbortSignal/Request.signal as Effect<void>. They complete immediately for already-aborted signals and register a once listener otherwise, with cleanup through Effect.async's returned finalizer.
asi.tradeoff: The helper only waits for abort; it does not prescribe racing/interruption policy or response shape. App handlers can choose how to compose it with their own Effects.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider a small documented example or helper showing race of long-running work against waitForRequestAbort, but avoid introducing broad cancellation policy until needed.

description: Abort racing helper attempt timed out when abort failure raced Effect.never

asi.hypothesis: Add minimal racing helpers withAbortSignal/withRequestAbort so handlers can fail long-running Effects with a typed RequestAbortError when clients disconnect.
asi.error_details: The test racing Effect.never against an abort-triggered failure timed out. Effect.raceFirst with a failing abort branch did not resolve as expected in this shape, likely because failure semantics/loser interruption were not appropriate for the intended helper.
asi.rollback_reason: Test timeout; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with a success-valued abort result or use Effect.raceWith/either carefully. Simpler option: keep wait helpers only and add a documented helper that maps abort to a success discriminant instead of a failure.

description: Success-valued abort race helper still timed out against Effect.never

asi.hypothesis: Use a success-valued Completed/Aborted discriminated union with disconnected race branches so handlers can compose abort races without failure semantics issues.
asi.error_details: The Aborted branch still timed out when racing against Effect.never, even after mapping abort to success and wrapping race branches with Effect.disconnect. Effect.never is a poor test target or raceFirst is not the right primitive for this helper shape.
asi.rollback_reason: Test timeout; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not ship a generic race helper yet. Reapply a smaller helper that maps AbortSignal/Request abort into a success-valued discriminant without racing arbitrary work, or first study Effect.raceWith semantics with a non-never interruptible task.

description: Expose abort reasons as composable Effects

asi.hypothesis: After two failed generic abort-race attempts, a smaller reliable helper should expose AbortSignal/Request abort reasons as Effects without racing arbitrary work.
asi.learned: abortSignalReason and requestAbortReason compose with the existing wait helpers and read signal.reason after abort, preserving custom disconnect reasons such as 'client closed' or 'gone'. This avoids the tricky Effect.raceFirst + Effect.never semantics that caused timeouts.
asi.tradeoff: No generic withAbort/race helper is shipped yet; apps can combine the reason Effect with their own Effect patterns once a concrete use case clarifies the right interruption semantics.
asi.next_action_hint: Move away from generic abort racing for now. Consider documenting streaming/disconnect lifecycle or adding higher-level response helpers for common error/status cases.

description: Support status and custom headers in HTML and direct Datastar responses

asi.hypothesis: HTML and direct Datastar response helpers should preserve safe default content types while allowing handlers to set HTTP status and custom headers for accepted/queued/error response cases.
asi.learned: htmlResponse now accepts ResponseInit and preserves caller headers/content-type overrides. htmlPatchResponse, jsonSignalsResponse, and scriptResponse accept init through their options, keeping Datastar-specific headers layered on top of custom status/headers.
asi.tradeoff: SSE response helpers remain unchanged because their call shape is variadic event strings; adding ResponseInit there needs a separate API decision. Direct single-shot responses now cover the common customization path.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider a separate sseResponseWithInit or eventStreamResponse option only if concrete examples need custom SSE status/headers; otherwise focus on docs or small file-backed client route composition.

description: Support status and custom headers in SSE response helpers

asi.hypothesis: SSE response helpers and realtime streams should offer the same status/custom header capability as direct responses while preserving required Datastar/SSE default headers.
asi.learned: sseHeaders now merges caller headers with text/event-stream, no-cache, and keep-alive defaults. sseResponseWithInit, patchElementsResponse/patchSignalsResponse init args, eventStreamResponse init, and liveElementsResponse init cover raw, Datastar patch, async, and live streaming responses.
asi.tradeoff: sseResponse keeps its existing variadic event-string API for compatibility; custom init uses the explicit sseResponseWithInit helper. This avoids ambiguous overloads while still enabling advanced headers/statuses.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider small response helpers for common typed errors/statuses, or document the now-complete direct/SSE response customization matrix.

description: Add file-backed Datastar client route composition helper

asi.hypothesis: Apps/examples that load /datastar.js should be able to pair exact app routes with the real self-hosted datastar.js file route without hand-writing route arrays, while keeping asset serving explicit.
asi.learned: datastarClientFileRoutes(filePath, ...routes) mirrors the in-memory datastarClientRoutes helper and composes directly with the exact-route router. A test verifies a full page route and the included ../datastar.js asset dispatch together through one router.
asi.tradeoff: The helper intentionally uses the default /datastar.js path only; custom path/cache options still use the explicit datastarClientFileRoute for now to avoid an overloaded composition API.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider adding an option bag to datastarClientFileRoutes only if custom path/cache composition is repeatedly needed; otherwise shift toward docs/examples or small route diagnostics.

description: No-any route/node typing attempt failed because unknown constraints lost router inference

asi.hypothesis: Remove public/internal any from route/node helper types and stop Node runtime helpers from erasing unprovided Effect context.
asi.error_details: Replacing Route<any, any> constraints with Route<unknown, unknown> caused router implementation to infer Effect<Response, unknown, unknown> and break the precise conditional return type. The test helper listen(app: ReturnType<typeof router>) also widened app context to unknown, conflicting with Node helpers requiring R=never.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure; reverted per autoresearch rules.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply in two smaller steps: first make Node runtime helpers require Handler<unknown, never> and fix tests with a better App type; leave route generic constraints alone or use a dedicated SomeRoute helper preserving inference without unknown widening.

description: Constrain Node runtime helpers to environment-free handlers without adding a scored runtime test

asi.hypothesis: Narrow the user-requested Effect-foundation fix to the runtime boundary: Node helpers should require Handler<unknown, never> and stop casting away unprovided Effect context.
asi.learned: The change typechecked and compile-time assertions could catch environment erasure, but the primary metric stayed unchanged because the new checks lived in an existing compile-time-only test block and did not add a scored runtime case.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric was unchanged; autoresearch rules discard equal primary metrics even for code-quality improvements.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the Node Handler<unknown, never> constraint with a small scored runtime test that asserts createNodeListener still serves environment-free handlers, and keep compile-time @ts-expect-error coverage for unprovided environments.

description: Stop Node helpers from erasing unprovided Effect context

asi.hypothesis: The most important immediate Effect-foundation fix is at the runtime boundary: Node helpers should only run handlers whose Effect context is already provided, instead of accepting any R and casting it to never.
asi.learned: createNodeListener, serve, and serveScoped now require Handler<unknown, never>; the unsafe cast in createNodeListener is gone. Compile-time coverage rejects handlers with unprovided context, while a real serve() regression verifies environment-free handlers still run without casts.
asi.tradeoff: Route composition still contains any-based constraints because a broad unknown replacement broke router inference. That should be revisited separately or replaced by Effect Platform HTTP primitives rather than forcing a brittle type trick.
asi.next_action_hint: Next investigate @effect/platform / @effect/platform-node HttpServer as the real replacement for the hand-rolled node:http adapter, ideally by adding dependencies and a small adapter or example rather than expanding raw Node plumbing.

description: Add Effect Platform HTTP adapter for ts-star handlers

asi.hypothesis: The prototype should not be locked to hand-rolled node:http plumbing; adding an adapter to @effect/platform HTTP apps lets ts-star handlers run under Effect's NodeHttpServer while preserving the Web Request/Response handler shape for now.
asi.learned: toPlatformApp converts the provided HttpServerRequest service to a Web Request with HttpServerRequest.toWeb, runs a ts-star Handler, then converts the Web Response back with HttpServerResponse.fromWeb. A real NodeHttpServer.makeHandler + node:http server test proves the adapter dispatches through Effect Platform.
asi.tradeoff: This is an adapter, not a full rewrite to HttpRouter/HttpApi yet. It keeps existing examples working while opening a migration path to Effect Platform. The raw node.ts adapter still exists and should be treated as compatibility/prototype plumbing, not the foundation.
asi.next_action_hint: Next replace or mirror the exact-route router on top of @effect/platform HttpRouter, or add tests for Effect Platform SSE/direct Datastar responses to ensure streaming semantics survive the adapter.

description: Convert exact ts-star routes to Effect Platform HttpRouter

asi.hypothesis: To make the foundation more idiomatic Effect, exact ts-star routes should be convertible to @effect/platform HttpRouter rather than only wrapped as one Web-style app.
asi.learned: toPlatformRoute maps a ts-star exact Route to HttpRouter.makeRoute via toPlatformApp, and toPlatformRouter builds an Effect Platform HttpRouter from route values. A NodeHttpServer.makeHandler test verifies GET, POST, and platform 404 behavior; invalid non-absolute paths fail early with PlatformPathError.
asi.tradeoff: The conversion still bridges through Web Request/Response for handler compatibility, and contains a narrow type assertion around HttpRouter.fromIterable inference. It is a migration path toward Effect Platform routing, not a complete rewrite of the app API yet.
asi.next_action_hint: Next validate Datastar SSE streaming through the Effect Platform adapter/router, or replace the remaining custom exact router internals with HttpRouter while preserving the simple public Route API.

description: Verify Datastar SSE streaming through Effect Platform router

asi.hypothesis: The Effect Platform adapter/router migration path must preserve Datastar long-lived SSE semantics, not just plain request/response behavior.
asi.learned: A toPlatformRouter route returning eventStreamResponse streams through NodeHttpServer.makeHandler with text/event-stream headers and delivers chunks before the body closes. This gives confidence that HttpServerResponse.fromWeb keeps Web Response streams viable for Datastar SSE over Effect Platform.
asi.tradeoff: This is still a bridge through Web Response rather than native HttpServerResponse constructors. The test validates the bridge while leaving a future refactor toward native platform responses open.
asi.next_action_hint: Next explore native @effect/platform response constructors for Datastar SSE/direct responses, or add a typed PlatformHandler surface that returns HttpServerResponse directly.

description: Add native Effect Platform Datastar SSE response helpers

asi.hypothesis: New Effect-first code should be able to return native @effect/platform HttpServerResponse values for Datastar SSE instead of always bridging through Web Response.
asi.learned: platformSseResponse, platformEventStreamResponse, platformPatchSignalsResponse, and platformPatchElementsResponse build native HttpServerResponse values with SSE defaults and optional status/custom headers. NodeHttpServer tests verify raw SSE, Datastar signal patches, rendered HTML element patches, and async SSE streams all work without Web Response conversion.
asi.tradeoff: These helpers currently cover SSE/patch responses only; direct HTML/JSON/script native platform helpers can follow if needed. Existing Web Response helpers remain for compatibility while Effect Platform becomes the preferred foundation.
asi.next_action_hint: Next add native Effect Platform direct response helpers for HTML/JSON/script or start migrating examples/tests to platform-native routes to reduce reliance on the custom Web router.

description: Add native Effect Platform direct Datastar response helpers

asi.hypothesis: Effect-first handlers should be able to return native @effect/platform HttpServerResponse values for single-shot Datastar actions (HTML patches, JSON signal patches, scripts) instead of relying on Web Response helpers.
asi.learned: platformHtmlResponse, platformHtmlPatchResponse, platformJsonSignalsResponse, and platformScriptResponse cover native direct responses with status/header support, rendered HTML nodes, Datastar override headers, JSON signal headers, and script attribute headers. NodeHttpServer tests prove they serve correctly through HttpRouter.
asi.tradeoff: Some implementation still mirrors Web helper behavior; future cleanup can factor shared header/default logic or move examples to platform-native handlers. This completes the native platform response surface enough to reduce raw Web Response dependence.
asi.next_action_hint: Next migrate one example (counter or search) to an Effect Platform-native route/router variant using platform response helpers, showing the preferred future foundation while keeping Web examples for compatibility.

description: Add Effect Platform-native counter example

asi.hypothesis: A platform-native counter example should demonstrate the preferred future foundation: Effect Platform HttpRouter/HttpServerResponse handlers using Datastar helpers, rather than building new framework design solely on Web Response wrappers.
asi.learned: examples/platform-counter.ts defines a native HttpRouter with a page route and increment action. The action reads HttpServerRequest.toWeb only at the signal-decoding boundary, returns native platformPatchSignalsResponse, and handles decode failures as a native 400 response. NodeHttpServer tests verify page rendering, good signal patches, bad signal errors, and route dispatch.
asi.tradeoff: Signal decoding still reuses the Web Request decoder, so the request layer is not fully platform-native yet. This is a deliberate incremental migration: native routing/responses first, then native signal decoding can follow.
asi.next_action_hint: Next add native Effect Platform signal decoding helpers using HttpServerRequest (query/body) to remove the remaining Web Request conversion inside platform-native actions.

description: Add native Effect Platform Datastar signal decoding

asi.hypothesis: Effect Platform-native actions should decode Datastar signals directly from HttpServerRequest instead of converting back to Web Request, removing the last compatibility bridge inside platform-native handlers.
asi.learned: platformRawSignalsFromRequest/platformReadSignalsFromRequest/platformReadSignals read GET/DELETE datastar query payloads or non-GET request text directly from HttpServerRequest, then reuse the existing JSON parse and Effect Schema decode pipeline. The platform counter action no longer calls HttpServerRequest.toWeb; tests cover POST, GET query, and typed decode failures through NodeHttpServer.
asi.tradeoff: The decode logic is duplicated conceptually with the Web request helper; a future refactor could share a pure raw-payload decoder. This is acceptable because platform-native handlers now avoid Web Request conversion at runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Next address remaining any/type-erasure in route composition with a smaller targeted approach, or migrate the custom exact router implementation to delegate to HttpRouter as the canonical runtime path.

description: Baseline current Effect v4 platform-native branch before docs-driven Stream/PubSub cleanup

asi.hypothesis: Establish the current post-Effect-v4, platform-native baseline before replacing any remaining manual streaming/pubsub primitives with Effect-native Stream/PubSub/Sink patterns from the local docs.
asi.learned: The current branch passes typecheck/tests with 111 prototype tests across 36 TS files. Earlier logged scores used a broader pre-cleanup workload, so this run acts as the current branch baseline for the docs-driven Effect-native pass.
asi.next_action_hint: Study Effect Stream/concurrency/sink docs, then target manual realtime/broadcaster helpers and async-iterator streaming paths for replacement with built-in Effect Stream/PubSub where it reduces custom plumbing.

description: First Effect PubSub realtime refactor failed typecheck on Effect.fork API/context inference

asi.hypothesis: Replace the manual Broadcaster/AsyncIterable realtime helper with Effect PubSub plus Stream.fromPubSub and Stream.map-based patching.
asi.error_details: Typecheck failed in realtime.test.ts: Effect.fork does not exist in Effect v4 beta API, and the attempted fork/join test inferred an unknown context for Effect.runPromise.
asi.rollback_reason: Typecheck failure before tests; autoresearch crash rollback required.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the PubSub refactor but use the v4 fiber API (`Effect.forkDaemon` or `Effect.forkScoped` if available) or avoid fibers in the broadcast test by using PubSub replay/current values. Keep the production code changes; the issue was test orchestration.

description: Replace manual realtime broadcaster with Effect PubSub and Stream.fromPubSub

asi.hypothesis: Effect already provides the right realtime primitives, so replacing the hand-rolled broadcaster/async-iterator queue with PubSub plus Stream.fromPubSub should reduce manual plumbing while preserving Datastar SSE behavior.
asi.learned: The local docs pointed directly to PubSub for broadcast fanout and Stream.fromPubSub for stream integration. The refactor removes custom subscription queues, maps live updates with Stream.map, keeps async iterables only at the outer response boundary for compatibility, and uses PubSub replay in the live counter to avoid subscribe-before-publish races.
asi.tradeoff: A small makeBroadcaster alias remains for compatibility, but it now returns an Effect PubSub instead of a custom class. Sink docs were useful for test consumption patterns but did not need production API changes in this slice.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue scanning for remaining manual stream/Effect integration. The next likely improvement is to make `platformEventStreamResponse` fully Effect-Stream-first in docs/examples, or add a scoped layer/resource constructor for realtime topics instead of calling Effect.runSync in createLiveCounter.

description: Add a runnable TSX counter example alongside hyperscript examples

asi.hypothesis: A TSX example will prove the existing JSX factory is practical for real Datastar/Effect Platform app code, not just isolated renderer tests.
asi.learned: `examples/tsx-counter.tsx` can use the same Datastar attribute helpers, Effect Schema signal decoding, native platform responses, and platform router as the hyperscript counter. TypeScript needed `examples/**/*.tsx` in tsconfig so the example is typechecked with the project.
asi.user_request: Add an example using TSX because current examples use hyperscript.
asi.tradeoff: This stays a thin TSX factory over the existing HTML node model; it does not introduce component semantics or a client framework.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue improving TSX ergonomics only where examples reveal friction. A possible next step is explicit support/tests for simple function components if desired, but avoid React-like scope creep unless it materially improves server-side Datastar views.

description: Support typed server components in the TSX factory and example

asi.hypothesis: A real TSX example becomes more useful if it can factor reusable typed server-side components instead of only using intrinsic tags.
asi.learned: The JSX factory can support minimal function components by passing cleaned props plus a single/array children prop, while keeping intrinsic elements rendered through the existing HTML node model. The TSX counter now uses a reusable typed CounterButton component without adding React-like runtime machinery.
asi.tradeoff: Component support is intentionally server-only and small: no hooks, lifecycle, or client framework semantics. A local cast is used at the factory boundary because TypeScript JSX needs generic component props while runtime dispatch only sees a function tag.
asi.next_action_hint: Next TSX ergonomics issue to investigate is whether attributes should use `class` only or also accept `className` as a server-side convenience; avoid adding React compatibility unless examples clearly benefit.

description: Add scoped realtime PubSub construction with automatic shutdown

asi.hypothesis: Effect's scoped resource pattern should manage realtime PubSub lifecycle directly instead of requiring every app/test to remember manual shutdown.
asi.learned: `makeRealtimePubSubScoped` composes the existing PubSub constructor with `Effect.addFinalizer` so closing the surrounding scope shuts down the PubSub. This follows the resourceful-stream/concurrency docs and gives apps a safer option for long-lived topics.
asi.tradeoff: The non-scoped constructor remains for examples/tests that intentionally own shutdown manually. The scoped helper is additive and keeps the PubSub/Stream foundation intact.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider updating live examples to use scoped construction when served by an Effect-managed runtime, or add a small test showing PubSub shutdown terminates stream readers without explicit shutdown calls.

description: Expose a scoped live counter constructor using scoped realtime PubSub

asi.hypothesis: The live counter example should model Effect-managed resource lifecycles by offering a scoped constructor that uses the scoped realtime PubSub helper rather than only a manually shutdown variant.
asi.learned: `makeLiveCounterScoped` reuses the same live counter assembly with `makeRealtimePubSubScoped`, so closing the surrounding Effect scope shuts down the PubSub. Tests verify the example-level scoped constructor releases its PubSub automatically.
asi.tradeoff: The existing `createLiveCounter`/`makeLiveCounter` helpers stay non-scoped for simple tests and demos that manually call `shutdown`, while Effect-managed runtimes can choose the scoped constructor.
asi.next_action_hint: Next promising cleanup: remove manual async generator test fixtures from platform streaming tests by using Effect Streams directly, and add Stream-based interval/live response examples if useful.

description: Normalize className in TSX examples to HTML class attributes

asi.hypothesis: After adding a TSX example, a small JSX factory normalization for `className` should remove a common TSX/server-rendering footgun while still emitting standard HTML.
asi.learned: The JSX factory can normalize intrinsic `className` to `class` without changing the underlying HTML node model. The TSX counter now demonstrates `className` in example code while rendering a correct `class` attribute.
asi.tradeoff: Only `className` is normalized for now. Broader React compatibility such as `htmlFor` is intentionally deferred until an example needs it.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue docs-driven cleanup by replacing remaining async-generator streaming examples/tests with Effect `Stream` constructors, or explore an Effect Stream/Sink test utility for collecting SSE responses.
